requirements.label: Historically limited to ages 17 to 29
requirements.source_quote: Applicants must be proficient in basic math and reading skills, have a high school diploma or GED, and be between the ages of 17-29.

data_quality_flags.note: This program is listed here specifically because a directory would list it and a person would waste a week on it. Three signals conflict. Secondary sources report the program stopped offering courses in 2023. The live site carries a 2026 copyright and Get Started and Join Now calls to action, implying it is active. But the site's own published contact details are unfilled template placeholders, which is not what an actively recruiting program looks like. This registry does not resolve the conflict. It surfaces it, and routes the person to a program they can actually start.

The age range comes from a third-party bootcamp review site, not from the program itself. It is recorded as unverified. If accurate, it would exclude many career changers, which is a material eligibility question and not a detail to discover after applying.

funding_paths.determined_by_source_quote: Local Alabama Career Centers provide WIOA (Workforce Investment Opportunity Act) scholarship opportunities to qualifying students for some workforce training programs. Eligibility is based on various factors, including income.

funding_paths.name: Pathways to Prosperity Scholarship
funding_paths.full_name: Pathways to Prosperity Scholarship, Alabama Community College System and the Paths for Success Foundation
funding_paths.administered_by: Alabama Community College System (ACCS) with the Paths for Success Foundation
funding_paths.covers: Up to $4,500 toward tuition, fees, books, credentialing fees, materials, and supplies for a short-term credential program
funding_paths.determined_by: The Alabama Community College System scholarship program, not the college's workforce office
funding_paths.determined_by_source_quote: Students must apply, receive approval, and agree to the scholarship terms and conditions.
funding_paths.provenance_note: The official ACCS scholarship page did not render fully for direct quotation during the build window. The details below are a faithful summary of that page, read twice, but they are recorded as paraphrase rather than verbatim quotation. Confirm the current terms on the ACCS page before relying on any of it.
funding_paths.why_it_matters_here: This is the only funding path found that could cover a Jefferson State Fast Track course outright. Fast Track is non-credit, and this scholarship explicitly covers non-credit short-term credential programs at Alabama Community College System institutions. Jefferson State is such an institution.
funding_paths.how_to_start: Read the terms on the ACCS scholarship page, then ask the college's workforce education office how students apply for it alongside a Fast Track registration.

who_it_is_for.group: Alabama residents entering a short-term credential program
who_it_is_for.why: The scholarship is for Alabama residents enrolling in a short-term credential program, for credit or non-credit, at an ACCS institution.

conditions: The program must be completable in two semesters or less.
The program must align with an in-demand occupation identified by the Alabama Committee on Credentialing and Career Pathways for the region where the college sits.
A student may not receive another award until a calendar year after completing the program the prior funds paid for.
unknowns: Whether the IT Help Desk course specifically appears on the in-demand occupation list for this region is not something this project can determine. That determination belongs to the scholarship program.
Whether a course running from November into February counts as within two semesters is a question for the college.

funding_paths.name: Vocational Rehabilitation Service
funding_paths.full_name: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services, Vocational Rehabilitation Service
funding_paths.covers: Individualized employment services including educational services and job training. The state page lists the service categories but does not itemise what costs are paid.
funding_paths.determined_by_source_quote: To be eligible for VRS services, individuals must: Be an Alabama resident; Have a physical or mental impairment that is a substantial impediment to employment; Must be able to benefit from services in terms of going to work.
funding_paths.why_it_matters_here: A disability that makes work harder is common and often undisclosed. This door is worth naming out loud precisely because people do not volunteer it, and because eligibility here does not turn on income.
funding_paths.how_to_start: Contact a local VRS office, or call the ADRS state office and ask for Vocational Rehabilitation Service.

who_it_is_for.group: People with a physical or mental impairment that is a substantial barrier to employment
who_it_is_for.why: This is the eligibility test the state publishes, alongside Alabama residency and being able to benefit from services in terms of going to work.
who_it_is_for.source_quote: Have a physical or mental impairment that is a substantial impediment to employment

contacts.name: ADRS, ask for Vocational Rehabilitation Service

unknowns: Whether tuition, fees, and books for a specific non-credit course are covered is not stated on the service page. An ADRS counselor decides what a given plan pays for.

funding_paths.name: SNAP Employment and Training
funding_paths.full_name: Alabama SNAP Employment and Training, administered by the Alabama Department of Human Resources
funding_paths.covers: Vocational and job training programs, plus supportive services including transportation and childcare
funding_paths.provenance_note: The DHR pages found during the build window describe this program from the vendor and procurement side rather than from the participant side. No participant-facing enrollment page was located. The program is real and the service list is quoted from a state page, but how a person actually enrolls could not be verified, so it is recorded as unconfirmed.
funding_paths.why_it_matters_here: The supportive services matter as much as the training money here. Transportation and childcare are the costs that quietly end a course in week three, and they are rarely covered by a training scholarship.
funding_paths.how_to_start: Ask a county DHR office about Employment and Training for food assistance recipients.

who_it_is_for.why: The program serves food assistance recipients and includes vocational and job training alongside supportive services.
who_it_is_for.source_quote: case management, transportation, childcare, and other participant expenses

unknowns: How a person enrolls, and whether the program is running with a vendor in Jefferson County right now, could not be confirmed from the pages found. Ask a county DHR office before relying on this.
